messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P2 - elevated 5xx rate for model v5-beta in us-west-2. Impact: ~8% error rate on gen endpoints, traffic spike from one heavy key. Alerting: latency and errors over SLO for 14m. Paging mica (oncall) and sam (eng-runtime).
mica (oncall): Acked. Investigating. Any quick blamestorm?
sam (eng-runtime): Looking at runtime logs now. Early sign: KV cache eviction thrash for v5-beta causing OOM-ish errors on a subset of workers. Repro on staging with same traffic pattern.
jordan (sre): Observed a burst of single-key fanout from key=k:heavy-retail. That key is sending large batch requests concurrently. We've got autoscale but some workers are overwhelmed -> 502s.
lina (prod): Customer-impact visible on dashboards: ~1200 requests/min to gen-v5 endpoints, 8% error rate, some downstream timeouts in CS dashboards. Karen, any active tickets?
karen (customer-support): Two customers opened tickets reporting failures ~10m ago. Marked as high. I asked for ETA for mitigation to tell them.
mica (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle offending key(s) 2) reduce v5-beta weight to 0 (route to v5-stable) 3) apply emergency per-key quota. I'm going to coordinate ops steps.
sam (eng-runtime): +1. Recommend disabling v5-beta variant from routing pool while we triage. We'll fail open to v5-stable which has same API.
ops-bot: Runbook step trigger: "Apply emergency key quota". To confirm, comment `apply_quota k:heavy-retail 5rpm`.
mica (oncall): Running throttles now.
mica (oncall): ```
# throttle heavy key
redwood ctl quota set --key "k:heavy-retail" --rate 5r/m --burst 2 --reason "emergency mitigation v5-beta errors"
```
ops-bot: Quota applied: k:heavy-retail -> 5r/m (burst 2).
jordan (sre): Quota enforcement active. We see immediate drop in sustained load from that key. Error rate trending down but still ~3.2%.
sam (eng-runtime): Initiating variant disable. Command:```
# demote v5-beta to 0 traffic
redwood routing update --model v5 --variant beta --weight 0 --reason "emergency disable due to elevated 5xx"
# verify
redwood routing get --model v5
```
ops-bot: Routing update queued.
mica (oncall): Executed routing update. Confirming traffic now shifting to v5-stable.
ops-bot: Routing table: v5-stable=1.0, v5-beta=0.0. All new requests routed to stable.
lina (prod): Noting: this is a non-destructive change but should stop the errors if beta is the root cause. Notify customers once we see <1% errors.
karen (customer-support): I'll update tickets: "We applied mitigations and routed traffic to stable variants; engineers are investigating".
ajex: (typo) Sorry ignore.
alex (eng-platform): Quick check: do we need to evict any quantized variants or purge caches to avoid stale state? Could be KV mismatch.
sam (eng-runtime): Good call. We'll clear per-worker KV caches for beta to avoid corrupt entries:```
# clear KV cache for nodes running v5-beta
redwood runtime exec --role worker --filter variant=beta --cmd "rm -rf /tmp/kv_cache/* && systemctl restart redwood-worker"
```
jordan (sre): Rolling restart scheduled across 6 nodes, one at a time. Doing node-1 now. Watching errors.
ops-bot: Node restart complete: node-1. No new 5xx spikes.
mica (oncall): Current status: error rate down to 0.9% across v5 endpoints, latency within SLOs. Heavy key quota holding. Routing to stable done.
lina (prod): Good. What's next? Do we keep beta disabled until root cause?
sam (eng-runtime): We should keep beta out of rotation until we reproduce and fix the KV eviction pattern. Tentative plan: repro in staging, patch memory handling, run soak test, then canary at low weight.
alex (eng-platform): Can we set a temporary global circuit-breaker for new non-auth keys to reduce blast radius if another key spikes? We have a policy toggle.
mica (oncall): Yes — enable emergency circuit-breaker for gen endpoints (limit per-key concurrent requests to 4). Executing:```
redwood safety set --circuit gen --per_key_concurrency 4 --reason "emergency - reduce blast radius"
```
ops-bot: Safety policy applied: gen per_key_concurrency=4.
jordan (sre): Monitoring for auth failures. No sign of downstream regressions.
karen (customer-support): Customers updated. One customer said they saw recovery and are ok for now.
lina (prod): Good. I'll schedule a postmortem runbook: RCA, timeline, follow-ups. Assign owners: sam to fix runtime leak, alex to add better KV metrics, mica to validate rollout policy tweaks.
mica (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing to night oncall jordan in 35m. Jordan, you have the follow-up POC and contact list.
jordan (sre): Ack. I'll take over and keep the circuit and quotas in place until the patch is deployed.
sam (eng-runtime): Quick note for after-hours: when we re-enable beta, do it with both: `weight=0.01` and `max_concurrency=2` per-key. Use canary band for 30m and watch error rate.
lina (prod): Also create a customer-facing incident summary once the RCA is ready. Karen will draft a short note.
karen (customer-support): Will do.
mica (oncall): Summary update: Mitigations executed: applied per-key quota to offending key, disabled v5-beta routing, cleared KV caches on beta workers, applied circuit-breaker. Impact reduced from 8% -> <1%. No data loss. Incoming tasks: reproduce in staging, patch eviction, improve KV observability.
alex (eng-platform): I'll add a Grafana panel for per-variant KV eviction rate and a routing audit log for quick lookups.
sam (eng-runtime): I'll start a staging repro now and post logs to the incident ticket.
jordan (sre): Night handoff complete. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. If anything flares, page the oncall.
mica (oncall): Thanks team. Closing incident thread for active mitigation — keeping thread open for RCA notes. :thumbsup:
